# Grab's Autonomous Vehicle Playbook for Singapore and Southeast Asia

**From:** The AV Market Strategist <avmarketstrategist@substack.com>  
**Date:** 2026-10-01T05:53:38.000Z

---

View this post on the web at https://avmarketstrategist.substack.com/p/grabs-autonomous-vehicle-playbook

Southeast Asia should be the last place AV's arrive. Dense, improvised traffic, monsoon rain and some of the cheapest driver labor in any middle-income region. Yet in April 2026, Punggol in northeast Singapore became the first residential neighborhood in Southeast Asia with a public autonomous passenger service.
In this episode of Autonomy Insiders, I talk with Dominic Ong, General Manager Autonomous at Grab, who runs that program with WeRide and Singapore's Land Transport Authority (LTA).
We cover:
→ Why Grab's case for autonomous vehicles is about reliability, not driver cost
→ How Grab's hybrid model dispatches autonomous vehicles and human drivers on one network
→ How Grab, WeRide and LTA split the work in Singapore
→ Why vehicle uptime now matters more than miles per critical intervention
→ What breaks an AV stack in Southeast Asia: vehicle costs in Singapore, monsoon rain, motorcycles and right-hand drive
→ Delivery robots, and why Grab takes equity in AV partners like WeRide, Momenta and Vay
→ How Grab views Waymo's planned entry into Singapore
